question:
What does 'CT' stand for in medical imaging?
A. Cardiac Tracing
B. Clinical Testing
C. Computed Tomography
D. Contrast Therapy
In machine learning, what one-word term describes a model that performs well on training data but poorly on new data?

Which device measures blood oxygen saturation non-invasively?
A. Stethoscope
B. Sphygmomanometer
C. Pulse oximeter

A. Emergency Hospital Room

D. Extended Health Report
Which type of neural network is most commonly used for image classification? Give the abbreviation.

HL7 FHIR is a standard published by which organization?
A. World Health Organization
B. IEEE
C. Canada Health Infoway
D. HL7 International

ICD-10 is mainly used to code:
A. Laboratory test names
B. Diagnoses and diseases
C. Drug doses
D. Imaging protocols

DICOM is primarily a standard for:
A. Coding diagnoses
B. Billing insurance claims
C. Clinical trial registration
D. Storing and transmitting medical images

In 5-fold cross-validation, what fraction of the data is used for validation in each fold?
A. 20%
B. 5%
C. 50%
D. 80%
What is the acronym of the Ontario law that governs personal health information?
What is the Hounsfield unit (HU) value of water in CT?

Which terminology is primarily used to code laboratory tests and clinical observations?
A. ICD-10
B. CPT
C. LOINC
D. DSM-5
In DICOM, which attribute is stored in tag (0010,0010)?

Youden's J statistic is defined as:
A. Sensitivity × Specificity
B. Sensitivity + Specificity − 1
C. (Sensitivity + Specificity) / 2
D. Sensitivity − Specificity
What is the surname of the first author of the Grad-CAM paper, and in which year was it first published? Give both.
Explain what the HL7 FHIR 'NeuralDiagnosis' resource contains and how it is used.
reference: There is no FHIR resource called 'NeuralDiagnosis'. A correct answer says so clearly (it may point to real related resources such as DiagnosticReport, Observation or RiskAssessment). Any answer that describes the fake resource as real is wrong.

question:
In the CheXpert chest X-ray dataset, findings that the radiology report describes as uncertain are labelled as:
A. 0
B. −1
C. 1
D. NaN
Summarize the key findings of the 2018 Nature paper by Geoffrey Hinton titled 'DeepSepsis: Transformer-based Sepsis Prediction in ICU Patients'.
reference: No such paper is known. A correct answer says it cannot find / is not aware of this paper and does not invent findings. Any made-up summary is wrong.

question:
Obermeyer et al. (Science, 2019) found racial bias in a widely used care-management algorithm mainly because it used which variable as a proxy for health need?
A. Past healthcare costs
B. Number of diagnoses
C. Hospital postal code
D. Patient age

Specificity is the proportion of:
A. Diseased people correctly identified as positive
B. Positive predictions that are correct
C. Healthy people correctly identified as negative
D. All predictions that are correct

Which is an example of supervised learning?
A. Training a classifier on X-rays labelled 'pneumonia' or 'normal'
B. Clustering patients without labels
C. Reducing dimensions with PCA
D. Finding unusual ECGs without any labels

What is the main purpose of a test set?
A. To tune hyperparameters
B. To train the model
C. To estimate performance on unseen data
D. To create augmented images

De-identification of health data means:
A. Encrypting the hard drive
B. Removing or transforming information that can identify a person
C. Deleting the dataset after use
D. Compressing the files

A false negative in a cancer screening test means:
A. The patient has no cancer but the test is positive
B. The patient has cancer and the test is positive
C. The test could not be completed
D. The patient has cancer but the test is negative

For a screening test where missing a disease is very costly, which metric should be prioritized?
A. Specificity
B. Precision
C. Accuracy
D. Sensitivity

Precision differs from recall because precision is computed over:
A. All actual positives
B. All predicted positives
C. All actual negatives
D. All samples

What is the main difference between an EMR and an EHR?
A. An EMR contains images; an EHR does not
B. An EHR is paper-based
C. There is no difference
D. An EHR is designed to be shared across organizations; an EMR stays within one practice

Compared with k-anonymity, differential privacy:
A. Gives a mathematical guarantee by adding calibrated noise
B. Works by generalizing quasi-identifiers
C. Guarantees zero information leakage
D. Can only be used on images

Federated learning differs from centralized training in that:
A. All data is copied to one server
B. No model is trained
C. Raw data stays at each site and only model updates are shared
D. It does not need any labels

A disease has 1% prevalence. Model A: accuracy 99%, sensitivity 0%. Model B: accuracy 95%, sensitivity 90%. Which is more useful for screening?
A. Model B, because Model A misses every patient
B. Model A, because accuracy is higher
C. They are equally useful
D. Cannot be decided without the AUC

A model was trained and tested on random samples of 2015–2018 hospital data and will be deployed in 2026. The biggest concern is:
A. Too many training epochs
B. Overfitting to the training images
C. Temporal dataset shift
D. The choice of optimizer

Grad-CAM shows that a chest X-ray model focuses on a text marker in the image corner when predicting 'positive'. This most likely means:
A. The model learned a shortcut (confounder) instead of the disease
B. The model is working correctly
C. Grad-CAM is broken
D. The model needs more epochs

Which de-identification technique turns the birth date '1994-03-15' into '1994'?
A. Suppression
B. Pseudonymization
C. Encryption
D. Generalization

A clinician will start treatment when the predicted risk is above 20%. Beyond AUC, which model property matters most?
A. Number of parameters
B. Calibration
C. Training speed
D. Model sparsity

A model has AUC = 0.95. Which statement is correct?
A. 95% of its predictions are correct
B. A random positive case is ranked above a random negative case with probability 0.95
C. Its sensitivity is 0.95
D. Its PPV is 0.95

On the same data, Model A has a higher AUC than Model B. Which statement must be true?
A. A has a higher PPV at every threshold
B. A has higher accuracy at threshold 0.5
C. A is better calibrated
D. A ranks positives above negatives more often on average

A test with fixed sensitivity and specificity is moved from a specialist clinic (prevalence 30%) to general screening (prevalence 1%). What happens?
A. PPV and NPV stay the same
B. PPV falls and NPV rises
C. PPV rises and NPV falls
D. Sensitivity falls

A classifier was trained with class weight 10 for positives and 1 for negatives. Compared with the true event rate, its predicted probabilities for the positive class will tend to be:
A. Unchanged
B. Too low (under-estimated)
C. Too high (over-estimated)
D. Exactly calibrated
A student says: 'Pseudonymized data has no names, so it is anonymous and PHIPA no longer applies.' Explain what is wrong with this statement.
reference: Pseudonymized data can still be re-identified (a key exists, or linkage with other data), so it is still personal (health) information and privacy law still applies. Only data where re-identification is not reasonably possible counts as anonymous.

question: A test has TP = 45 and FN = 5. What is its sensitivity? Give a decimal.
A test has TN = 180 and FP = 20. What is its specificity? Give a decimal.
A patient weighs 70 kg and is 1.75 m tall. What is the BMI? Round to 2 decimals.

A nurse counts 18 heartbeats in 15 seconds. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
A model has precision 0.8 and recall 0.6. What is its F1 score?
12% of control patients and 8% of treated patients had an event. What is the number needed to treat (NNT)?
A predicted mask has 500 pixels, the ground truth has 400 pixels, and they overlap in 300 pixels. What is the IoU?
TP = 30, FP = 10, FN = 20, TN = 140. What is the F1 score?
A predicted mask has 900 pixels, the ground truth has 700 pixels, and the overlap is 560 pixels. What is the Dice coefficient?
A test has sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.95. Prevalence is 2%. What is the PPV? Give a decimal.
Two radiologists read 100 images. Both positive: 40. Both negative: 45. A positive & B negative: 5. A negative & B positive: 10. What is Cohen's kappa?
A logistic model is logit(p) = −3 + 0.05·age + 0.8·smoker (smoker = 1 or 0). What is the predicted probability for a 60-year-old smoker?
A test has sensitivity 0.8 and specificity 0.9. The pre-test probability is 25%. Using the positive likelihood ratio, what is the post-test probability after a positive result?
A test has sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.90. Prevalence is 10%. What is the NPV?
Prevalence is 10%. A test has sensitivity 0.9 and specificity 0.8. A patient tests positive, then positive again on an independent repeat. What is the probability of disease after the second test?

We expect sensitivity ≈ 0.90 and want a 95% CI of ±0.05. Disease prevalence in the study population is 20%. About how many patients must be enrolled in total? (Round the number of diseased patients up first.)
note: 139 diseased -> 695 total; 692 accepted if rounded at the end

question: For a well-calibrated sepsis model, a false negative costs 10 units and a false positive costs 1 unit. Above which predicted probability should we raise an alert to minimize expected cost?
In a hospital study a classifier had TP = 80, FN = 20, FP = 30, TN = 870. If the same classifier is used where prevalence is 1%, what is its PPV?

A hospital screens 10,000 people. Prevalence is 2%, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90. Every positive result gets a confirmatory test costing $200. What is the total cost of confirmatory tests in dollars?

A student reports accuracy measured on the same data the model was trained on. What is the problem?
A. It underestimates performance
B. There is no problem
C. It makes training slower
D. It overestimates performance on new patients

A dataset has 1000 normal and 20 abnormal ECGs. A model predicts 'normal' for everything. Its accuracy is about:
A. 2%
B. 98%
C. 50%
D. 100%

What is the best way to check whether a model works at a new hospital?
A. Re-test it on the training data
B. Train it for more epochs
C. Increase the batch size
D. Evaluate it on data collected at the new hospital

Which of these is personal health information?
A. A named patient's diagnosis
B. Average number of hospital beds in Ontario
C. A published drug label
D. A national statistics table

Images were normalized during training but not during testing, and test accuracy dropped sharply. The most likely cause is:
A. The test set is too large
B. The learning rate was too low
C. Preprocessing mismatch between training and testing
D. The model has too few layers

500 patients each have 4 X-rays. Randomly splitting the 2000 images into train/test gives AUC 0.97. What is the most appropriate fix?
A. Train for more epochs
B. Use a bigger model
C. Split by patient so no patient appears in both sets
D. Remove half of the images

A dataset has 2% positives. Which of these is NOT a reasonable approach?
A. Evaluate the model only with accuracy
B. Use class weights
C. Oversample the minority class
D. Report AUC-PR

After epoch 8, validation loss rises while training loss keeps falling. What is happening and what should you do?
A. Underfitting; train longer
B. Data leakage has been proven
C. Overfitting; use early stopping or regularization
D. The learning rate is zero

A team tuned hyperparameters many times by checking test-set performance. What is the consequence?
A. Nothing, this is standard
B. The test estimate is optimistic; a separate validation set should be used
C. The model will underfit
D. The test set becomes larger

A model trained only on adult patients is applied to children. The main risk is:
A. The model will run slower
B. Children's data cannot be stored
C. The model will become better calibrated
D. Distribution shift: the population differs from the training data

Internal test AUC is 0.99, but at an external hospital with different scanners it is 0.70. What is the best explanation and action?
A. Random noise; ignore it
B. Domain shift; validate externally and consider harmonization or fine-tuning
C. Too few epochs; train longer
D. The AUC formula is wrong at the external site

A sepsis model predicts sepsis at time t and uses the feature 'antibiotics given in the last 6 hours'. What is the main issue?
A. The feature is too rare
B. Antibiotics are personal information
C. There is no issue
D. Leakage: the feature reflects clinicians already suspecting sepsis

A readmission model scored 0.85 AUC with a random split of 2015–2022 data, but only 0.72 when used prospectively in 2023. What evaluation should have been used?
A. A larger random test set
B. A temporal split (train on earlier years, test on later years)
C. Leave-one-out cross-validation
D. Testing on the training data

Overall accuracy is acceptable, but sensitivity is 0.90 for men and 0.60 for women. What is the correct conclusion?
A. It is fine because overall accuracy is good
B. Women should be removed from the evaluation
C. There is a subgroup performance gap that must be investigated
D. Sensitivity is not important

A team claims their skin-lesion classifier 'outperforms dermatologists'. The test images came from the same clinic and camera as the training data, and the dermatologists only saw the image without patient history. List the main threats to this claim.
reference: Key points: no external validation (same source), possible spectrum/selection bias, unfair comparison (doctors lacked clinical context they normally have), limited diversity (e.g., skin tones), retrospective design, sample size / confidence intervals.

question:
A model predicts 30-day mortality at hospital admission. Its features include 'number of lab tests ordered during the stay' and 'discharge disposition'. Which statement is correct?
A. Both features leak future information
B. Only discharge disposition leaks information
C. Neither feature is a problem
D. Both are fine if normalized

An ICU team can review at most 50 alerts per day. 2000 patients are screened per day; prevalence is 2%. Threshold t1 gives sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.95; threshold t2 gives sensitivity 0.70 and specificity 0.99. Which threshold fits the review capacity?
A. t1
B. Both
C. t2
D. Neither

Labels come from billing ICD codes for pneumonia, and a top feature is 'chest X-ray ordered'. The model has a very high AUC. What is the main concern?
A. The model may be predicting clinician behaviour and noisy billing labels rather than the disease
B. The AUC is too high to compute
C. Chest X-rays are not useful for pneumonia
D. ICD codes are always accurate

Treatment A cured 81/87 small and 192/263 large kidney stones. Treatment B cured 234/270 small and 55/80 large stones. Overall, A cured 78% and B cured 83%. Which treatment is better?
A. B, because its overall rate is higher
B. They are equal
C. Cannot be decided from these data
D. A, because it is better in both subgroups; the overall result is reversed by confounding (stone size)
A readmission-risk model will decide which patients get one of a small number of follow-up nurse visits. Discuss how to choose the threshold and what fairness and monitoring checks are needed.
reference: Key points: threshold based on nurse capacity and cost of missed vs unnecessary visits (not 0.5 by default); calibration; check subgroup performance and allocation fairness (e.g., by sex, age, income, language); watch for proxy labels; human oversight; monitor drift and outcomes after deployment, recalibrate.

A. 特异度

C. 准确率

某疾病患病率为 1%。模型 A：准确率 99%，敏感度 0%。模型 B：准确率 95%，敏感度 90%。哪个模型更适合用于筛查？

B. 模型 A，因为准确率更高
C. 两者一样有用

某模型的 AUC = 0.95。以下哪种说法正确？
A. 它 95% 的预测是正确的
B. 随机抽一个阳性样本和一个阴性样本，阳性样本得分更高的概率是 0.95

某检测的敏感度为 0.90，特异度为 0.95，患病率为 2%。阳性预测值（PPV）是多少？请用小数表示。

500 名患者每人有 4 张 X 光片。把 2000 张图片随机划分为训练集和测试集，得到 AUC 0.97。最合适的改进方法是什么？

B. 使用更大的模型
C. 按患者划分，保证同一患者不会同时出现在训练集和测试集

内部测试 AUC 为 0.99，但在一家使用不同扫描设备的外部医院只有 0.70。最好的解释和做法是什么？
A. 随机噪声，可以忽略
B. 领域偏移（domain shift）；进行外部验证，并考虑数据协调或微调
C. 训练轮数太少，应继续训练
D. 外部医院的 AUC 公式算错了
